advances:
This is a complete rational counterexample to the requested
unit-dominated, argmin-supported endpoint/kink disintegration.  Even after
one copy of every full horizontal section at an endpoint or kink height is
allowed as an atomic marginal, every admissible argmin measure has mass at
most \(38\), whereas the two required positive masses are
\(N-H=40\) and \(|Q^+|=3\,003\,392/9\,025\).  The registered lower
functional is nevertheless positive on this triple.  Thus this packet
refutes only the proposed disintegration mechanism, not the lower-functional
inequality and not the locked three-slice theorem.
author: mp_r165_support_atom_transport
proof:
Every point of \(A_0\) has \(x\le-20\) and \(|y|\le19\), while a
vertical section of \(A_2\) at \(0\le x\le400\) is
\[
\left[-\frac{x}{400},\frac{x}{400}\right].
\]
Therefore \(A_0\subset\mathcal L\) and
\(A_2\subset\mathcal R\).  The cyclic vertices of \(B\) are
\[
\left(-\frac{2\,885}{19},-\frac{19}{2}\right),
\left(\frac{915}{19},-10\right),(190,-10),(190,10),
\left(\frac{915}{19},10\right),
\left(-\frac{2\,885}{19},\frac{19}{2}\right),
\]
which proves \(B\subset K\).  Direct area calculation gives
\[
|A_0|=38\left(\frac{5\,770}{19}-20\right)=10\,780,
\]
\[
|A_2|=400,\qquad |K|=386\cdot20=7\,720.
\]
This proves (2), including \(M>k>m>0\) and \(0<t<M\).

Reflection in the \(x\)-axis interchanges the two diagonal caps of
\(K\).  More explicitly,
\[
\int_{-10}^{10}(190+y)\,dy
=\int_{-10}^{10}(190-y)\,dy
=3\,800,
\]
which proves (3).  Also
\[
C=197\cdot20=3\,940,\qquad C-\pi=140.
\]
The tail cut is
\[
x\ge\delta+2=\frac{5\,808}{19}.
\]
Integrating the vertical section length \(x/200\) of \(A_2\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta
&:=\left|A_2\cap\left\{x\ge\frac{5\,808}{19}\right\}\right|\\
&=400\left(1-\left(\frac{5\,808}{7\,600}\right)^2\right)
=\frac{1\,501\,696}{9\,025}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
Since the complementary tail area is \(m-\theta\), equations
(2) and (19) give (4).

For \(a_0\in A_0\) and a tail point \(a_2\in A_2\),
\[
x\left(\frac{a_0+a_2}{2}\right)
\ge\frac{-\delta+(\delta+2)}2=1,
\]
which proves (8).  On \(A_0\), both \(x+y\) and \(x-y\) are at most
\(-1\).  On \(A_2\), both are nonnegative, vanish only at the origin,
and have positive-area sublevel strips at the origin.  This proves that
both origin contacts are genuine lower crossings.

The set \(Y\) is
\[
Y=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,1),(1,10),(10,10)\}.
\]
The only part added when passing from \(B\) to \(G\) is the triangle
with horizontal base from \(x=1\) to \(x=915/19\) and height \(1/2\).
Hence
\[
|G\setminus B|
=\frac12\left(\frac{915}{19}-1\right)\frac12
=\frac{224}{19}.
\]
Each diagonal hull excess is at most this total excess, proving (5).
The minimum of either transformed coordinate on \(K\) is
\(-196-10=-206\), so \(\alpha=\beta=206\), and direct substitution
gives (6).  This completes the normalized-hypothesis verification.

The transformed polygons are
\[
P=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
(39,1),
\left(\frac{6\,131}{19},\frac{5\,409}{19}\right),
\left(\frac{5\,409}{19},\frac{6\,131}{19}\right),
(1,39)
\right\},
\]
\[
Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(399,401),(401,399)\}.
\tag{20}
\]
Both nonzero vertices of \(Q\) come from points of \(A_2\) with
\(x=400>\delta+2\), proving (10).  Since \(D\) has absolute
determinant \(2\), equation (19) proves (7).

The lower endpoint of a horizontal section of \(Q/2\) lies on the
edge from \((0,0)\) to \((399/2,401/2)\).  Hence
\[
\gamma_-(z)=\frac{399}{401}z,
\qquad 0\le z\le\frac{401}{2}.
\tag{21}
\]
The right endpoint of a horizontal section of \(P\) is
\[
p_+(\eta)=
\begin{cases}
\eta+38,
&1\le\eta\le\dfrac{5\,409}{19},\\[2mm]
\dfrac{11\,540}{19}-\eta,
&\dfrac{5\,409}{19}\le\eta\le\dfrac{6\,131}{19}.
\end{cases}
\]
Since \(E=-P/2\), its lower endpoint is
\[
e_-(y)=-\frac12p_+(-2y)
=
\begin{cases}
-\dfrac{5\,770}{19}-y,
&-\dfrac{6\,131}{38}\le y\le-\dfrac{5\,409}{38},\\[2mm]
y-19,
&-\dfrac{5\,409}{38}\le y\le-\dfrac12.
\end{cases}
\tag{22}
\]

At fixed output height \(v=z+y\), the exact infimal-convolution
objective is
\[
\frac{399}{401}z+e_-(v-z).
\]
On the first branch of (22) its slope in \(z\) is
\[
1+\frac{399}{401}>0,
\]
while on the second branch it is
\[
\frac{399}{401}-1<0.
\]
Thus the minimizer is unique at every output height and is
\[
z_*(v)=
\begin{cases}
0,
&-\dfrac{6\,131}{38}\le v\le-\dfrac{5\,409}{38},\\[2mm]
v+\dfrac{5\,409}{38},
&-\dfrac{5\,409}{38}\le v\le\dfrac{1\,105}{19},\\[2mm]
\dfrac{401}{2},
&\dfrac{1\,105}{19}\le v\le200.
\end{cases}
\tag{23}
\]
This proves (12).  It also shows that every probability kernel supported
on the argmin fiber over \(v\) is forced to be
\[
\kappa_v=\delta_{(z_*(v),\,v-z_*(v))}.
\tag{24}
\]
The right side of (24) is Borel measurable by (23).

The two endpoint sections of \(\mathcal C\) in the vertical branches
of (12) are points, so
\[
w_{\mathcal C}(0)
=w_{\mathcal C}\left(\frac{401}{2}\right)=0.
\tag{25}
\]
At the complementary kink height, the corresponding \(P\)-section is
\[
\left[\frac{4\,687}{19},\frac{6\,131}{19}\right]
\times\left\{\frac{5\,409}{19}\right\}.
\]
The homothety by \(1/2\) therefore gives
\[
w_E\left(-\frac{5\,409}{38}\right)
=\frac12\left(\frac{6\,131-4\,687}{19}\right)=38.
\tag{26}
\]

Let \(\Pi\) satisfy (12)--(14).  Its restriction to the first vertical
segment in (12) gives an atom at \(z=0\) in its
\(\mathcal C\)-height marginal.  By (13), (14), and (25), that
restriction has zero mass.  The same argument at \(z=401/2\) kills the
third segment.  All remaining mass lies on the middle segment
\(y=-5\,409/38\).  Equations (13), (14), and (26) then give
\[
\|\Pi\|
\le\nu_E\left(\left\{-\frac{5\,409}{38}\right\}\right)
=38.
\]
This proves (15).  Extra atoms at the other endpoint and kink heights
listed in \(\mathcal Z,\mathcal Y\) do not alter the conclusion: the
only nonvertical argmin segment is at \(y=-5\,409/38\), and the two
vertical segments have already been killed by (25).

More explicitly, if \(\lambda\) is a finite positive measure on the
output heights and \(\kappa_v\) is any probability kernel supported on
the argmin fiber, then
\[
\Pi(A)=\int\kappa_v(A)\,d\lambda(v)
\]
has total mass \(\|\Pi\|=\|\lambda\|\).  Thus preserving either
required mass forces \(\|\Pi\|=N-H\) or
\(\|\Pi\|=|Q^+|\), respectively, contradicting (7), (15), and
(16).

If a measure is first assigned to the full horizontal sections, its
projection to the two height coordinates is a measure \(\Pi\) on
\(\Gamma\).  Unit domination by planar area plus one copy of every full
special section projects exactly to domination by (13).  Thus the
preceding argument already allows full-section horizontal smearing.
Assigning mass \(40\) to the complementary kink section would reuse that
section with multiplicity at least
\[
\frac{40}{38}=\frac{20}{19}>1,
\]
and assigning \(|Q^+|\) requires multiplicity at least
\[
\frac{|Q^+|}{38}
=\frac{1\,501\,696}{171\,475}>1.
\tag{27}
\]
This proves the claimed marginal obstruction.

It remains to verify the two required masses and the positive functional
calibration.  In original coordinates, the negative transformed quadrant
is \(x\le-|y|\).  Therefore
\[
H=2\pi=7\,600,
\]
\[
N=2\int_{-10}^{10}(196-|y|)\,dy=7\,640.
\]
This proves (16), and (7) then gives (17).

For \(v\le0\), a horizontal section of \(K'\) has right endpoint
\[
r(v)=v+20.
\]
Consequently
\[
J=[-9,0].
\tag{28}
\]
On \(J\), equation (23) gives
\[
a_W(v)=\frac{399}{401}v-\frac{150\,170}{7\,619},
\]
and \(a_W(v)<2-v\).  Direct integration gives
\[
\int_J
\left(5(2-v)-a_W(v)-4r(v)\right)\,dv
=-\frac{364\,284}{7\,619}.
\tag{29}
\]
For \(v>0\), the cut \(2-v\) lies between the endpoints of the
\(W\)-section precisely for
\[
0<v<\frac{5\,169}{475}.
\]
On this interval,
\[
2-v-a_W(v)
=\frac{165\,408-15\,200v}{7\,619};
\]
afterward the positive part is zero.  Hence
\[
5\int_{v>0}
\left[\min\{b_W(v),2-v\}-a_W(v)\right]_+\,dv
=\frac{427\,496\,976}{723\,805}.
\tag{30}
\]
Adding (29) and (30) proves (18).

Finally, the actual forced-tail midpoint body
\[
R=\frac{Q^+-P}{2}
\]
is two-dimensional.  Its height projection has endpoints
\[
\frac12\left(
\frac{399}{400}\frac{5\,808}{19}-\frac{6\,131}{19}
\right)
=-\frac{4\,219}{475}<0,
\qquad
\frac{401-1}{2}=200>0.
\]
Thus \(R\) has positive area in each open halfplane \(v<0\) and
\(v>0\).  The obstruction is therefore present away from \(T=0\) and
away from both zero-half strata.  Since (18) is positive, no conclusion
about the lower-functional inequality or the main theorem follows from
this counterexample.
statement:
Let
\[
\mathcal L=\{(x,y):x\le-|y|\},\qquad
\mathcal R=\{(x,y):x\ge|y|\},\qquad
\mathcal U=\{(x,y):y\ge|x|\},
\]
and take
\[
\delta=\frac{5\,770}{19},\qquad
A_0=[-\delta,-20]\times[-19,19],
\]
\[
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(400,-1),(400,1)\},
\qquad
K=[-196,190]\times[-10,10].
\tag{1}
\]
Put
\[
B=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},\qquad
M=|A_0|,\quad m=|A_2|,\quad k=|K|,
\]
\[
t=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9,\qquad \pi=t-m,\qquad
C=|K\cap\{x\le1\}|,
\]
\[
Y=K\cap\mathcal U\cap\{x\ge1\},\qquad
G=\operatorname{conv}(B\cup Y),
\]
and let
\[
D(x,y)=(u,v)=(x+y,x-y),\qquad
P=-D(A_0),\quad Q=D(A_2),\quad K'=D(K).
\]
The triple (1) satisfies all complete strict normalized support-contact
hypotheses.  Its exact data include
\[
M=10\,780,\quad m=400,\quad k=7\,720,\quad
t=4\,200,\quad \pi=3\,800,\quad C=3\,940,
\tag{2}
\]
\[
|K\cap\{x+y\ge0\}|=|K\cap\{x-y\ge0\}|=\pi,
\tag{3}
\]
\[
C+m-t=140>0,
\qquad
t-C-\left(m-\frac{1\,501\,696}{9\,025}\right)
=\frac{238\,196}{9\,025}>0,
\tag{4}
\]
\[
|G\setminus B|=\frac{224}{19}
<3\,700=\pi-\frac m4,
\tag{5}
\]
and, with
\[
\alpha=-\min_{K'}u,\qquad \beta=-\min_{K'}v,
\]
\[
\alpha=\beta=206,\qquad
7C+2\pi-2k-4\alpha\beta=-150\,004<0.
\tag{6}
\]
Both diagonal contacts in \(Q\) are the origin and are genuine lower
crossings.  The forced tail
\[
Q^+=D\!\left(A_2\cap\{x\ge\delta+2\}\right)
\]
has
\[
|Q^+|=\frac{3\,003\,392}{9\,025}.
\tag{7}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac{A_0+(A_2\cap\{x\ge\delta+2\})}{2}
\subseteq B\cap\{x\ge1\}.
\tag{8}
\]

For the contact \(q_v=(0,0)\), put
\[
\mathcal C=\frac{\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup Q^+)}2,
\qquad E=-\frac P2,\qquad W=\mathcal C+E.
\tag{9}
\]
Both nonzero vertices of \(Q\) belong to \(Q^+\), so
\[
\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup Q^+)=Q,\qquad
\mathcal C=\frac Q2,\qquad W=\frac{Q-P}{2}.
\tag{10}
\]
If \(\gamma_-(z)\) and \(e_-(y)\) are the lower endpoints of the
horizontal sections of \(\mathcal C\) and \(E\), define the full
height-argmin correspondence
\[
\Gamma=
\left\{(z,y):
\gamma_-(z)+e_-(y)
=a_W(z+y)\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
For this triple,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma={}&
\left\{0\right\}\times
\left[-\frac{6\,131}{38},-\frac{5\,409}{38}\right]\\
&{}\cup
\left[0,\frac{401}{2}\right]\times
\left\{-\frac{5\,409}{38}\right\}\\
&{}\cup
\left\{\frac{401}{2}\right\}\times
\left[-\frac{5\,409}{38},-\frac12\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]

For a horizontal section, write
\[
w_{\mathcal C}(z)
=\mathcal H^1(\mathcal C\cap(\mathbb R\times\{z\})),
\qquad
w_E(y)=\mathcal H^1(E\cap(\mathbb R\times\{y\})).
\]
The endpoint and kink heights of these two section-width functions are
\[
\mathcal Z=\left\{0,\frac{399}{2},\frac{401}{2}\right\},
\]
\[
\mathcal Y=
\left\{-\frac{6\,131}{38},-\frac{5\,409}{38},
-\frac{39}{2},-\frac12\right\}.
\]
Define the unit full-section augmented height measures
\[
\nu_{\mathcal C}
=w_{\mathcal C}(z)\,dz
+\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}
w_{\mathcal C}(\zeta)\delta_\zeta,
\]
\[
\nu_E
=w_E(y)\,dy
+\sum_{\eta\in\mathcal Y}w_E(\eta)\delta_\eta.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus (13) contains the ordinary Cavalieri area marginals and, at every
endpoint or kink height, one atom whose mass is the length of the entire
actual horizontal section.

For every finite positive measure \(\Pi\) supported on \(\Gamma\) whose
two coordinate marginals satisfy
\[
(\operatorname{pr}_z)_\#\Pi\le\nu_{\mathcal C},
\qquad
(\operatorname{pr}_y)_\#\Pi\le\nu_E,
\tag{14}
\]
one has
\[
\|\Pi\|\le38.
\tag{15}
\]
The same bound applies to any measure on the full products of the
horizontal sections whose height projection is supported on \(\Gamma\)
and whose two body marginals are unit-dominated by planar area plus one
copy of every full endpoint/kink section.

On the other hand, with
\[
H=|K'\cap\{v\ge0\}|,\qquad
N=|K'\cap\{u\le0,\ v\le0\}|,
\]
this triple has
\[
H=7\,600,\qquad N=7\,640,\qquad N-H=40>38,
\tag{16}
\]
and
\[
T=|Q^+|-(N-H)
=\frac{2\,642\,392}{9\,025}>0.
\tag{17}
\]
Consequently no measure satisfying (11)--(14) can preserve either
required positive mass \(N-H\) or \(|Q^+|\), so no such
unit-dominated probability-kernel disintegration can preserve them
simultaneously.

This is not a counterexample to the registered lower functional.  If
\[
I_{K'}(v)=[\ell(v),r(v)],\qquad
J=\{v\le0:r(v)\ge2-v\},
\]
then its exact value is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_J
\left(5(2-v)-\min\{2-v,a_W(v)\}-4r(v)\right)\,dv\\
&\qquad
+5\int_{v>0}
\left[\min\{b_W(v),2-v\}-a_W(v)\right]_+\,dv\\
&\hspace{45mm}
=\frac{392\,889\,996}{723\,805}>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
The actual forced-tail midpoint body \((Q^+-P)/2\) has positive area
on both \(v<0\) and \(v>0\).  Thus the marginal obstruction occurs
with \(T>0\), with both required masses positive, and with both
placed-tail halves nonzero.
